title: Evaluation on a weakly contractible affine preserves limits and colimits of modules
statement:
Let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and let $W$ be an affine
weakly contractible object. Then $\Gamma(W,-)$ from $\mathcal R$-modules to
$\mathcal R(W)$-modules preserves all limits and all colimits. In particular, for every
family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ the map $\bigoplus_iM_i(W)\to(\bigoplus_iM_i)(W)$ is an
isomorphism, and $\Gamma(W,-)$ commutes with filtered colimits.

proof.text: Work in the fixed universes and a small skeleton of the pro-étale site; all diagrams and families below are small in the universe in which their colimits are formed. By the sectionwise-limit lemma, for any diagram $(M_a)$ its limit has sections $\{(m_a)\in\prod_a M_a(V): M(u)(m_a)=m_b\text{ for all }u:a\to b\}$. Setting $V=W$ identifies the limit cone with the limit cone of $\mathcal R(W)$-modules. Thus evaluation preserves all limits, including the empty limit and kernels. No weak contractibility is needed for this part.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, limit construction; Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2)

proof.text: For a family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ form the presheaf of modules $P(V)=\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i(V)$ with componentwise restrictions. The sectionwise-presheaf-colimit lemma makes $P$ the coproduct of the underlying module presheaves. Let $\eta:P\to Q=P^\#$ be module sheafification. A morphism $Q\to H$ to a module sheaf is, by the sheafification universal property, exactly a presheaf morphism $P\to H$, and hence exactly a family of module-sheaf morphisms $M_i\to H$. Consequently $Q$, with the maps induced by the summand inclusions, is the coproduct in module sheaves. This identifies the canonical comparison in the statement with $P(W)\xrightarrow{\eta_W}Q(W)$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, colimit construction, using Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules

proof.text: For each finite subset $J\subset I$, the presheaf $F_J(V)=\bigoplus_{j\in J}M_j(V)=\prod_{j\in J}M_j(V)$ is a module sheaf: glue each of the finitely many coordinates separately, and uniqueness follows coordinatewise. The coordinate projection $P\to F_J$ extends uniquely to $r_J:Q\to F_J$ by module sheafification. The composite $i_J:F_J\hookrightarrow P\xrightarrow{\eta}Q$ satisfies $r_Ji_J=\mathrm{id}_{F_J}$, as is checked on every section before sheafification. Hence $i_J(V)$ is injective for every object $V$. This proves the subsheaf assertion needed for descent without presuming that evaluation preserves an infinite sum.

source.place: Direct sums, finite subsum paragraph; elementary split-inclusion proof in place of the sheafification-exactness argument

proof.text: Let $s\in Q(W)$. Module sheafification is abelian-group sheafification, whose underlying sets are set sheafification by the cited comparison. The local-sections theorem therefore gives a covering $\{V_k\to W\}$ and $p_k\in P(V_k)$ with $\eta(p_k)=s|_{V_k}$. Apply the affine finite-cover-refinement lemma to the covering sieve generated by these arrows. Its finite covering family $\{T_l\to W\}_{l\in L}$ consists of arrows in that sieve, so each factors through some $V_k\to W$; restriction gives $p'_l\in P(T_l)$ lifting $s|_{T_l}$. Each $p'_l$ has finite support, and their union over finite $L$ is a single finite $J\subset I$. Regard all $p'_l$ as sections of $F_J$. After restriction along any pair of arrows from a common object into two covering members, they have the same image in $Q$, namely the restriction of $s$; the sectionwise injectivity of $i_J$ from step 3 makes them equal in $F_J$. The sheaf condition glues them to $t\in F_J(W)$. Its image in $Q(W)$ is $s$ by separatedness. Thus $\eta_W$ is surjective. This argument also applies to an empty covering of the empty object: both sheaves have their unique zero section there.

proof.text: If $x\in P(W)$ maps to zero in $Q(W)$, its support is contained in a finite $J\subset I$. Then $x$ is the image of $t\in F_J(W)$ and $i_J(W)(t)=0$; applying the retraction $r_J(W)$ gives $t=0$, hence $x=0$. Together with step 4 this proves that $\eta_W$ is a bijective $\mathcal R(W)$-linear map, hence an isomorphism. It is exactly the coproduct comparison from step 2, so evaluation preserves arbitrary direct sums, including the empty sum. For a map between two families its comparison square commutes on each summand by the definition of $\eta$; the coproduct universal property then gives commutativity.

source.place: Direct sums, injectivity paragraph; compatibility with summand maps written out

proof.text: We now prove preservation of cokernels for the full weak-contractibility hypothesis in the statement. Let $f:M\to N$ be a morphism of module sheaves, set $A(V)=N(V)/f_V(M(V))$, and let $C=A^\#$ with $q:N\to C$. The definition of module sheaves identifies $q$ as a cokernel; its underlying sheafification is abelian-group sheafification and hence set sheafification by the cited comparisons. The local-sections theorem shows that $q$ is locally surjective as a map of sheaves of sets: locally a section of $C$ comes from a class in $A$, which has a representative in $N$. By the set-sheaf epi criterion, $q$ is an epimorphism on underlying set sheaves. Let $K=\ker q$, computed sectionwise by the limit lemma. For $n\in K(V)$, the class of $n$ and zero in $A(V)$ have equal image in $A^\#(V)$. The local-equality clause of the local-sections theorem gives a covering on which this class is zero, so on each covering member $n$ is $f(m)$ for some section $m$. Thus $M\to K$ is also locally surjective on underlying set sheaves, hence an epimorphism there. Condition (3) of weak contractibility makes both $N(W)\to C(W)$ and $M(W)\to K(W)$ surjective. Since $K(W)=\ker q_W$, it follows that $\ker q_W=f_W(M(W))$ and $q_W$ induces the canonical isomorphism $N(W)/f_W(M(W))\cong C(W)$. Therefore evaluation preserves cokernels. This proves the exactness consequence for every weakly contractible $W$, without imposing that its coordinate ring be w-contractible.

proof.text: For a small diagram $D:\mathcal I\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal R)$, let $B=\bigoplus_{a\in\mathrm{Ob}\mathcal I}D(a)$ and $A=\bigoplus_{u:a\to b}D(a)$. Define $d:A\to B$ on the summand for $u:a\to b$ by $\iota_bD(u)-\iota_a$, and let $q:B\to L$ be its cokernel. A map $h:B\to H$ is a family $h_a:D(a)\to H$; the condition $hd=0$ says, on the summand for each $u:a\to b$, exactly $h_bD(u)=h_a$. By the cokernel universal property such families factor uniquely through $L$. Thus $L$ with the maps $q\iota_a$ is the colimit of $D$. For the section diagram, put $B_W=\bigoplus_aD(a)(W)$ and $A_W=\bigoplus_{u:a\to b}D(a)(W)$, define $d_W$ on the $u$-summand by $x\mapsto\iota_bD(u)_W(x)-\iota_a(x)$, and set $L_W=B_W/\operatorname{im}d_W$. For an $\mathcal R(W)$-module $H$, a linear map $B_W\to H$ is a family $h_a:D(a)(W)\to H$. It factors uniquely through $L_W$ exactly when it kills every displayed relation, equivalently when $h_bD(u)_W=h_a$ for every arrow $u$. Thus $L_W$ with the quotient coprojections is the module colimit, including the empty diagram, for which $A_W=B_W=L_W=0$.

source.place: Colimits paragraph, explicit maps and verification of the presentation by its universal property

proof.text: Under the direct-sum comparisons of steps 2–5, the map $d(W)$ of step 7 is the map on direct sums of $\mathcal R(W)$-modules whose component for $u:a\to b$ sends $x$ to $\iota_bD(u)_W(x)-\iota_a(x)$: evaluation preserves addition and composition of module-sheaf maps sectionwise. Step 6 identifies $L(W)$, with its quotient map, with the cokernel of this map. By the universal-property computation in step 7, it is the colimit of $a\mapsto D(a)(W)$, with the same structure maps. Thus the resulting isomorphism is the canonical colimit comparison. If a morphism of diagrams is given, the two comparison composites agree on each structure map $D(a)(W)$, and so are equal by the colimit universal property. In particular evaluation commutes with filtered colimits, and step 1 supplies all limits as required.
